claims.text: Applying a thin, dense Al2O3-based ceramic coating to RHEAs will improve their high-temperature oxygen resistance.
The Al2O3-based coating will limit oxygen ingress by acting as a diffusion barrier.
The applied coating will form a continuous and adherent layer on the alloy.
The continuous coating layer will inhibit oxygen diffusion and slow oxidation kinetics in the underlying alloy.
At high temperature, the Al2O3 coating will develop a stable, slow-growing oxide scale.
The slow-growing oxide scale will impede further oxygen ingress and reduce the oxidation rate.
Reduced oxidation will lessen degradation of the alloy microstructure and mechanical properties.
Coated RHEAs will have lower oxidation-induced mass gain than untreated RHEAs.
Coated RHEAs will develop thinner oxide scales than untreated RHEAs.
Coated RHEAs will retain mechanical properties better than untreated RHEAs after high-temperature exposure.
Untreated RHEAs typically oxidize rapidly at high temperatures.
High-temperature oxidation of untreated RHEAs typically causes significant mass gain and thick, non-protective oxide scales.
High-temperature oxidation of untreated RHEAs typically deteriorates their mechanical properties.
The coating is predicted to remain effective at approximately 1000°C during about 100 hours of continuous exposure to air or pure oxygen.
Performance above approximately 1000°C or during thermal cycling may be limited by coating spallation or degradation.
Optimal coating thickness, deposition parameters, and long-term adhesion under repeated thermal cycling are not established.
